roles.heroLead: Renton has two kinds of bathrooms: the ones in Boeing-era ramblers on Talbot Hill and Kennydale, and the ones in townhomes that went up on the hillsides last decade. Different framing, different subfloors — the same rule applies to both. Grout is not a water barrier. We build the bonded assembly underneath, run a 24-hour flood test with photos, and only then open the first box of tile.

roles.costH2: How much does tile installation cost in Renton, WA?
roles.costP1: Figure $14–$26 per square foot installed for Renton tile work once tile, setting materials, prep and labor are all on the ticket — the labor line by itself opens at $11/sq ft. A standard tub-shower surround lands in the $3,200–$6,800 window, and a complete bathroom — floor, shower, niche — most often finishes between $6,500 and $14,000.
roles.costP2: Here is the part that catches Renton homeowners off guard: the shape of the tile matters more than its price tag. Penny rounds at $4 a foot can out-cost a $12 large-format plank on the invoice's labor line, because installers are paid for cuts and grout joints, not for what the tile store charged.
roles.costNote: Renton installed ranges, current for August 2026 — tile, materials and labor combined. The number you can hold us to is the written one from the free estimate.
roles.layersLead: A shower is seven layers deep, and only the top one is visible. In the Renton failures we get called to open up, one hidden layer was skipped — nearly always the membrane, nearly always to shave a few hundred dollars off a job that later costs five figures to tear back apart.
roles.whyP1: Leaks in a 1962 Kennydale rambler and a 2019 hillside townhome announce themselves the same way: not at all. Water slips past grout, loads the substrate, and turns up seasons later as a springy hallway or a shadow on the ceiling under the bath. At that point you are buying framing, subfloor, drywall and a second tile job.
roles.whyP2: The waterproofing layer runs roughly ten percent of a shower's price. In any era of Renton house, cutting it is the most expensive line item you can remove.
roles.scopeIntro: These are floor prices, not final ones — format, substrate condition and layout complexity all push them. The number that counts gets written at your house, free.
roles.cardShower: The complete waterproofed build: pre-sloped pan, bonded membrane, overnight flood test, then niche, curb or curbless entry and tile. What you are really buying is the part that disappears behind the wall.
roles.cardFloors: Bathroom, kitchen, entry, laundry, basement — flattened first, with an uncoupling membrane wherever an older Renton subfloor moves or a heat mat goes down.
roles.cardBacksplash: From plain subway to herringbone to slab-look panels. We cut clean around outlets, trim the edges properly, and match grout to your counter rather than the sample board.

roles.faqQ1: How much does tile installation cost in Renton, WA?
roles.faqA1: In Renton, installed tile runs about $14 to $26 per square foot with tile, setting materials, substrate prep and labor counted together; labor alone starts at $11 per square foot. Tub-shower surrounds come in around $3,200 to $6,800, while a full bathroom with floor, shower and niche generally totals $6,500 to $14,000. Format is the real price lever — mosaic sheets and oversized planks each demand far more labor per foot than a standard 12×12.
roles.faqQ2: How much does it cost to tile a shower in Renton?
roles.faqA2: Budget $3,200 to $6,800 for a standard alcove shower in Renton — demolition, the bonded waterproofing system, a pre-sloped pan, tile setting, a niche and grout are all inside that number. Curbless thresholds, benches, steam setups and full-height stone climb from there. Waterproofing is only about a tenth of the total, and it is the piece standing between you and a five-figure tear-out.
roles.faqQ3: Do you waterproof showers before tiling?
roles.faqA3: Every time, no exceptions. Behind our tile goes a bonded system — never bare cement board with thinset over it. Pre-sloped base, membrane up the walls, sealed corners, seams and penetrations per TCNA / ANSI A118.10, then the drain gets plugged, the pan filled, and the whole thing sits under water for 24 documented hours before tile day. Tile and grout shed water; only the membrane actually stops it.
roles.faqQ4: How long does a bathroom tile job take?
roles.faqA4: Four to six working days is normal for a Renton bathroom: demolition and dust protection first, then substrate and waterproofing with the overnight flood test, one or two days of setting, and a final day of grout, silicone and trim. The shower needs 24 more hours of cure before its first use. A floor by itself is usually a one- or two-day job.
roles.faqQ5: Porcelain or ceramic tile — which is better?
roles.faqA5: For anything wet or walked on, porcelain — it is denser, takes on under 0.5% water, and shrugs off impacts that chip ceramic. Ceramic earns its keep on walls and backsplashes at a lower price. Our Renton spec is porcelain for every floor and shower floor; ceramic and glass compete for the vertical surfaces.
roles.faqQ6: Can you install a heated tile floor?
roles.faqA6: Yes — an electric radiant mat under the tile adds roughly $11 to $16 per square foot installed, thermostat included. It goes over an uncoupling membrane, gets resistance-tested twice — before and after the tile is set — and draws from a dedicated circuit. The moment to say yes is while the floor is already open; retrofitting means paying for demolition twice.
roles.faqQ7: Do I need to remove the old tile first?
roles.faqA7: Usually, yes. At about $3.50 per square foot including haul-away, demolition is also your only honest look at the subfloor — rot, movement, and where the finished height needs to land at doorways. Tiling over old tile is occasionally fine on a dead-flat, well-bonded surface, but it lifts the floor and buries problems better found now than after grout.
roles.faqQ8: How much does a kitchen backsplash cost in Renton?
roles.faqA8: A Renton kitchen backsplash typically prices at $1,100 to $2,200 for a standard run near 30 square feet, with outlet cutouts, edge trim and color-matched grout included. Mosaics, herringbone, framed details behind the range and full-height slab-look porcelain occupy the top of the range because layout and cutting time drive the labor.
roles.faqQ9: Can you fix cracked tile or regrout instead of replacing?
roles.faqA9: Often. Repair and regrout work starts at $8 per square foot and makes sense when grout has stained or crumbled, an impact cracked a tile or two, or shower corners need the grout cut out for silicone. But hollow-sounding tile, pieces loosening in a spreading pattern, or a wall with give means the substrate has failed — a patch there only rents you time, and we will say which case is yours before quoting.
roles.faqQ10: Which Renton neighborhoods do you tile?
roles.faqA10: All of them — the Renton Highlands and East Renton Highlands, Kennydale, Benson Hill, Fairwood, Talbot Hill, Maplewood, Downtown, Cascade, Tiffany Park, Liberty Ridge, Rolling Hills, Earlington, President Park, Renton Hill and Skyway — plus neighboring Newcastle, Bellevue, Mercer Island, Issaquah and Seattle.
roles.faqQ11: What warranty comes with tile installation?
roles.faqA11: Tile work from OC Flooring carries a 2-year workmanship warranty — double our carpet term, because tile problems surface in year two rather than week two. Install a manufacturer's complete waterproofing assembly and their system warranty stacks on top, and since we photograph the membrane and the flood test, the documentation exists whenever you sell the house.
